{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "---
name: release-please

"on":
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  release-please:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: googleapis/release-please-action@v5
        id: release
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.PORTER_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        if: ${{ steps.release.outputs.release_created }}

      - name: Build and publish to GitHub Package
        uses: actionshub/publish-gem-to-github@main
        if: ${{ steps.release.outputs.release_created }}
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          owner: ${{ secrets.OWNER }}

      - name: Build and publish to RubyGems
        uses: actionshub/publish-gem-to-rubygems@main
        if: ${{ steps.release.outputs.release_created }}
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.RUBYGEMS_API_KEY }}
",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs on every push to main and performs release and gem publishing. Historical runs show consistent success with durations around 24-30 seconds. Adding a custom job timeout (5 minutes) bounds runaway executions without affecting valid runs, preserving all intended functionality. This optimization is supported by the literature pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (reported VM time reduction up to 12.9% free / 8.1% paid) and the experimental evidence for history-based timeouts (experiment:batch-ishara-pattern-bat-a14b642d809bf336) which added a 5-minute timeout to similar jobs. The change is minimal, safe, and does not weaken permissions or add privileged actions.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-ishara-pattern-bat-a14b642d809bf336"]
}
